title: Coherent states in quantum billiards constructed in the basis of the continued eigenfunctions
authors: I. D. Burkov, S. S. Seidov
abstract: In the article a new approach to construction of generalized coherent states in quantum billiards is proposed. The coherent states are defined as the projections of a Gaussian wave function on the basis of the eigenstates of the quantum billiard, continued outside. The continuation is built as the solution of the equivalent Balian--Bloch equation, defined on the entire $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the projection operator is built using the resolvent of the Balian--Bloch equation. In the case of the one--dimensional potential well and billiards, belonging to the Coxeter group, the wave functions of the coherent states were expressed analytically via the Jacobi and Riemann theta functions.
summary: This paper introduces a novel method to construct generalized coherent states for quantum billiards by reformulating the problem using the Balian–Bloch integral equation defined on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This approach successfully bypasses the mathematical discontinuities that arise when restricting standard eigenfunction expansions to the physical boundaries of the billiard. It provides an advanced theoretical tool for analyzing quantum dynamics in confined spaces.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical construction of generalized coherent states for quantum billiards, specifically overcoming the boundary discontinuity issues inherent in standard eigenfunction expansions.
main_result: The authors propose defining these coherent states using projections onto a basis derived from the solution of the Balian–Bloch integral equation, which correctly handles the boundary conditions.
method: The core method involves extending the problem from the bounded domain $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ by formulating an equivalent Balian–Bloch integral equation, which is then used to define the projection operator and the coherent state wave function.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum particle confined within a quantum billiard ($\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$), governed by the free particle Hamiltonian with Dirichlet boundary conditions. The analysis is extended to 1D infinite potential wells and 2D Coxeter billiards.
key_observables: The coherent state wave function $\Psi_c(r, t)$, the projection operator $P$, and the propagator $G(r, r', t)$.
important_parameters: The boundary $\partial\Omega$, the Gaussian wave packet parameters, and the short-time limit $t 	o 0^+$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that extending the problem to $\mathbb{R}^2$ via the Balian–Bloch equation provides the correct physical description, thereby avoiding boundary discontinuities encountered in standard expansions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerically obtained coherent states in various billiard geometries, showing the difference between the state away from the boundary and near the boundary, and comparing results from infinite limits versus finite partial sums to highlight boundary effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the limitations of standard eigenfunction methods, then introducing the Balian–Bloch equation as a generalization, deriving the coherent state via projection, and finally applying this framework to solvable models like the 1D infinite well using special functions (Jacobi/Riemann theta functions).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for defining quantum states in confined geometries, which is crucial for understanding boundary effects in quantum dynamics relevant to AMO physics and mesoscopic systems.
